name: Locked-Camera Split Mask Illusion
use_when: A subject should disappear behind an object, peek from another side, or appear as a clone in a locked-off shot.
The footage includes a clean plate or compatible takes from the same locked camera position.
Manual focus, exposure, white balance, and camera position can be kept constant.
avoid_when: The camera moves between takes or auto exposure/focus changes the image.
The split line crosses moving shadows, reflections, people, or changing background detail.
The actor crosses the mask boundary in a way that reveals the composite.
The illusion could mislead in documentary or evidence-based contexts.

timeline_pattern.pattern: locked_camera_plate -> action_take_or_clone_take -> trim_best_takes -> overlay_take_above_plate -> split_mask_aligned_to_object_edge -> time_dialogue_or_action -> preview_boundary -> add_foley_or_room_tone
timeline_pattern.capture_rule: Lock exposure, focus, white balance, and camera position before filming the clean plate and action takes.
timeline_pattern.mask_rule: Align the split mask to a real vertical/horizontal object edge when possible, such as a pole, wall, door, or furniture line.
timeline_pattern.timing_rule: For clones, record multiple takes and choose lines/reactions that interlock cleanly before masking.
timeline_pattern.sound_rule: Foley such as footsteps or door movement can sell the illusion only after the visual timing works.

motion.rule: The mask boundary should feel locked to the environment, not animated unless the boundary object moves.

keyframe_values.plate_duration: Capture enough clean plate before action so the editor has timing handles.
keyframe_values.mask_angle: Set split-mask angle to match the object edge; 90 degrees works only when the edge is truly vertical.
keyframe_values.take_repeats: Record multiple dialogue/action takes because clone timing is hard to repair later.
keyframe_values.boundary_review: Review the mask boundary at full playback speed after any brightness or color adjustment.

sound.rule: Use room tone continuity and subtle foley to make the composite feel like one space; keep dialogue timing natural.

captions.rule: Captions should not cover the mask boundary when the viewer needs to see the illusion.

color.rule: Both sides of the split must match in brightness, focus, white balance, and grain/noise; avoid auto camera changes during capture.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use overlay with crop/alpha masks for the active side over a clean plate, align takes by frame, and use color matching filters only for small corrections.
implementation.remotion: Represent takes with plateRef, actionTakeRef, maskLine, maskFeather, syncFrame, dialogueCueFrames, and boundaryReviewFrames.
implementation.blender: Use video planes or compositor layers with a split alpha mask aligned to the environment; add spatial audio/foley if rendering a scene.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Film a locked clean plate and action takes, trim the plate as the base, make the action take an overlay, apply Split mask, rotate/position it to the object edge, align timing, and preview for exposure/focus mismatch.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Stack clean plate and action/clone takes, use opacity masks or track mattes aligned to object edges, feather only if needed, and use audio tracks/room tone to blend takes.

common_mistakes: Leaving auto exposure or auto focus on during capture.
Moving the camera between the clean plate and action takes.
Aligning the split mask to an arbitrary line instead of a believable object edge.
Choosing clone takes that talk over each other or leave unnatural reaction gaps.
Adding foley before the visual composite is timed.
qc: Were camera position, focus, exposure, and white balance locked?
Does the mask boundary align with a real object or plausible seam?
Do both sides match in brightness, focus, and color?
Does the actor avoid crossing the mask boundary in a revealing way?
Do clone lines, reactions, and foley feel synchronized?
